title: Ang 300–317: Gauri ki Var M4
hook: including the Gursikh's daily routine on ang 305
tomorrow: what makes a day a good one?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thiti: every day is his, whatever shape the moon is in. Today, a ballad, and a Sikh's whole day on one page.

Morning-routine videos: the alarm at five, the cold water, the journal, the green drink, all filmed from a tripod. Simran's dad has had a routine since before those videos existed: up in the dark, a shower, the Japji, then the yard before the trucks roll. The test is in two days, and this week Simran has been getting up with him. Not for the drink. For the quiet. On Ang 305, in Gauri ki Var, Guru Ram Das wrote out a whole day of a Sikh of the Guru.
screen: `ALARM AT FIVE, TRIPOD ON.` → `UP IN THE DARK WITH DAD.` → `A SIKH'S DAY, ON ANG 305.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase: whoever calls themself a Sikh of the True Guru rises early and meditates on the Name. They make the effort in the early hours, bathe, and wash in the pool of nectar. They repeat the Name as the Guru teaches, and their troubles fall away. Then, through the day, they sing Gurbani, and with every breath and every bite, they remember. And the closing line: Nanak asks for the dust of the feet of the Gursikh who repeats the Name, and helps others repeat it too. Notice three things. It isn't a performance; nobody's filming. It isn't only the morning; it runs through the whole day, breath and bite. And it isn't for yourself alone; the last line is about helping someone else remember. That's the difference between a routine and a practice. A routine is built to improve you. This one, by the end, has turned you outward. For Simran's week, what it gives is something steady under the nerves: the day before a test starts the same way as any other. And it closes a loop. Ang 156 was the alarm, a night lost in sleep. Ang 305 is what waking up is for.
screen: `RISE EARLY, REMEMBER THE NAME.` · `THROUGH THE DAY: BREATH AND BITE.` · `HELP SOMEONE ELSE REMEMBER.` · `A ROUTINE, OR A PRACTICE?` · then, large: `THE DAILY ROUTINE.`

segments.voice: Plan tomorrow's first five minutes the way you'd plan a trip. Name what you want them to hold, a breath, a line, a moment of quiet, and then the one thing most likely to steal them, probably your phone. Decide now: when I reach for it, I'll sit up and take three breaths first.
Ang 300: where Guru Ram Das's ballad in Gauri begins; on Ang 305, a Sikh's whole day, start to finish.
Your line: the daily routine. It starts in the dark, and it ends with helping someone else remember. Bye for now.

notes: v3 storyline (days 1471–1484): Simran is learning to drive in the yard of her dad Harjit's trucking company, with the test at the end of the second week.
